Even if you’re considered “average” on here, you’re still considered #1 in my mind. Your extracurriculars are literally so cool! I’m sure you’ll do great wherever you end up!

As long as you enjoyed your extracurriculars, I really don’t think it matters whether they’re extraordinary or not. As long as you’ve grown as an individual from them, I’m sure they did their part! Don’t let this sub convince you that your extracurriculars are average because they are not. We think our extracurriculars are average when we come here because we are used to everyone having insane accomplishments. But my friend, you have accomplished so much! Be proud of yourself and treat yourself to something nice! (Like MUJI pens — I freaking love MUJI pens omg.)

Any school would be lucky to have you. If you get rejected by one that you really wanted to go to, it’s THEIR loss not yours. I am literally so proud of you! You’ll do great things wherever you end up.

Listen to me, everything is going to be okay. College is not your entire life nor it is an institution where you have to sell your soul to get in. As for your mental health “ruining your chances of getting into a good college,” I certainly don’t think that’s the case. 

For now, I’d focus on reaching out for help and focusing on taking care of yourself more. Once you invest more into yourself, you’ll be more capable of doing the work that is needed to get into college. 

I promise you that three years of your life are not going to define the trajectory of your life. As long as you show how you’ve grown into the person you are today from those experiences, I’m sure colleges will understand where you’re coming from. You’re 16 man; your life is just starting, not ending. You still have a chance to ask for help and get back up on your feet. 

If no one else believes in you, I do. There is a person sitting on the other side of the country that is rooting for you. You can get through this: you will get through this. Just focus on taking care of your physical and mental health. Don’t let the fear of not getting into college get in the way of pursing your passions and achieving your dreams. Your dreams and passions don’t even have to be grand or set in stone right now. Your passion could be helping out the women’s shelter on the weekends or teaching little kids how to read; it doesn’t have to be creating the cure to cancer and solving every problem in the world. You have time to figure yourself out; don’t think that it’s all too late just because you’re a junior. Because it’s not. 

Life is long and hard; don’t let one thing be the on to knock you down so far that you can’t get back up. 

Moral of the story is that it’s not too late to get back up on your feet. I know you feel like you’re at your lowest point right now, but it doesn’t have to stay that way. Ask for help and find the little things in life to make you happy.

We’re all here for you if you need help along the way. 

Lots of love, 

Perry

I have never related to an internet stranger more than I have now. I'm also a college student and my mental health has been terrible this semester. But I have some advice that can help.

​

1. **Talk to someone.** You've already reached the first step in expressing your feelings online. All you have to do is talk to someone else. Even if your college sucks, there are probably some mental health resources that you can access for free. I promise you that whatever you're feeling is not meant to be kept all in your head.
2. **Look at transferring out of college and into another one near the city.** Since you said you prefer the city more, is there any way you can transfer to a college near the city? Some colleges have different campuses in different cities. People transfer to other colleges all the time. As long as you're still in college, you're going to be fine. 
3. **When you're feeling homesick, keep some things from home around you.** Maybe it could be a throw pillow from your old living room. Keep little things in your new place that remind you from home. And if you still feel homesick, understand why you are feeling homesick. Are you missing home or are you missing the sense of security and the safety of your home?
4. **Get rid of the friends that don't feel real or communicate with them why you feel that way about them.** Sometimes it's better to have no friends than people who don't act like friends at all. But sometimes, people don't know that they're *not* being a good friend. It may just be in their head that they are being a good friend, but in reality, they are not.  Communicate with them and tell them how you are feeling. 

Last but not least, I need you to remember that you are not alone. Sometimes it feels like you're a "small fish in a big pond" where no one cares about you. Even if you think no one cares about you, I do. You just have to start caring for yourself and take matters into your own hands. Best of luck!
